units.translation: upon their shields they carry griffin-eagles wrought in bronze,
for the sharp-mouthed, silent hounds of Zeus, the griffins, you must guard.
and he crosses the city of Teuthras of the Mysians and the Lydian valleys (thus Hermann for τε γύαλα [and the fields]).

which could hardly have been written by Aeschylus, since immediately follows πολεμίας ὑπὸ χθονός [under hostile earth]. For this reason Ritschl conjectured τόνδε πιανῶ γύην [I will enrich this field], an emendation which the very word πιανῶ [I will enrich] in some way confirms. τόνδε γύην [this field] could have been written τήνδε γύην [this field] by the usual error of scribes, to which a glossator substituted χθόνα [earth]. Thus in Prometheus line 369 λευροὺς γύας [smooth fields], which M preserved, in all copies is written λευράς γύας [smooth fields]. Euripides used the singular in Heracl. 839 τὸν Ἀργείων γύην σπείροντες [sowing the field of the Argives].
